Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-52-N-8506 asserting that on 09.08.2023 at about 2.15 p.m. when petitioner riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA-18-EG-3034 on Tumkur - Bengaluru NH-48, near Agarwal Bhawan Mohammed Feezan vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20168685/

sentences.text:
1 Hotel, Adakamaranahalli, Dasanapura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, driver of Car bearing No.KA-52-N-8506, drove the same negligently, without furnishing any signal/indicator, came towards left side, made the motorcycle to dash the rear part of the car, thereby caused accident,
caused injuries to the petitioner.

2. Petitioner took treatment at Dhanavanthri hospital, Nelamangala and Bhagavan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru by spending Rs.8,00,000/-, as on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 33 years, used to earn Rs.30,000/p.m. by working as Office Incharge.

3. Regarding accident Nelamangala traffic police registered crime No.343/2023 against the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-52-N-8506.
4.

In response to the notice respondent No.1 insurance company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the reason and mode of accident nature and consequences of injuries suffered by petitioner.
5. In spite of service notice, respondent No.2 owner of Car bearing No.KA-52-N-8506 remained absent.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 10.07.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 09.08.2023 at about 2.15 p.m. on Tumkur- Bengaluru NH-48, near Agarwal bhavan hotel, Adakamaranahalli village, Dasanapura Hobli,
Nelamangala Taluk, in view of the negligent use of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-52-N-8506 accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
7. On 10.07.2024, 25.07.2024, 17.09.2024 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 11 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.11.

On 28.10.2024, 25.11.2024 petitioner produced the evidence of MRD of Bhagawan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Madan- complainant and Dr. S.A. Somashekara as PW2 to 4 and get produced 9 documents at Ex.P.12 to P.20.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues and additional issue are as under:
Issue No.1 ...

In view of negligent use of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-18-EG- 3034 by the petitioner and negligent use of the Car bearing No. KA-52-N- 8506 by Nagaraju at the ratio of 50:50 accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner.

Mohammed Feezan vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20168685/
2

sentences.text: Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.3,77,181/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 09.08.2023 at about 2.15 p.m. when riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA-18-EG-3034 on Tumkur - Bengaluru NH-48, near Agarwal Bhawan Hotel, Adakamaranahalli, Dasanapura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, driver of Car bearing No.KA-52-N-8506, drove the same negligently, without furnishing any signal/indicator, came towards left side, made the motorcycle to dash the rear part of the car, thereby caused accident,
caused injuries to the petitioner.
11. In the written statement respondent No.1 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
12. In the cross-examination petitioner stated that when he was riding the motorcycle, car overtook his motorcycle dashed to the motorcycle and submitted ignorance about the name of the complainant.
PW.1 stated that the people who are present in the spot filed complaint at Nelamangala Police Station.
PW.1 denied the suggestion that in view of his negligent riding of the motorcycle the accident taken place and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the car.

PW.1 admitted that after investigation police have filed charge sheet against himself and driver of the car for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
13.

In the evidence PW.2- MRD Assistant of Bhagawan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru produced copy of the police intimation, MLC register extract at Ex.P.13 and P.14.
14.
In the evidence affidavit PW.3-Madan M. S/o Muniraju stated that he has filed complaint pertaining to Crime No.343/2023 of Nelamangala Traffic Police Station.

PW.3 further stated that on 09.08.2023 at about 2.30 p.m. Mohammed Feezan (petitioner) was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-18-EG-3034 on Bangalore- Tumkur NH-48, near Adakamaranahalli village, near Agarwal Bhavan Hotel, all of a sudden driver of a Car bearing No.KA-52-N- 8506 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, overtook another vehicle suddenly took car to extreme left side of the road,
under that process petitioner lost control over the vehicle (motorcycle).
PW.3 stated that due to the majority neglect of the driver of the car the accident taken place.

In the evidence PW.3 produced copy of his Aadhaar card at Ex.P.18.
15.
In the cross-examination PW.3 submitted that during the accident he was not present in the place of accident and public have informed about the accident through mobile.
16. In the evidence affidavit PW.4 - Dr. S.A.Somashekara stated nothing about the reason and mode of the accident.

Mohammed Feezan vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20168685/
3 17.

sentences.text: Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.343/2023 registered on 09.08.2023 by Nelamangala Traffic police against the petitioner- Mohammed Feezan - rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-18-EG-3034 and Nagaraj- driver of Car bearing No.KA-52-N-8506 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPCon the basis of the complaint presented by PW.3- Madan S/o Muniraju.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of spot mahazar.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of motor vehicle accident report.

Ex.P4 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Nelamangala traffic police in crime No.343/2023 against the petitioner- Mohammed Feezan - rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-18-EG-3034 and Nagaraj- driver of Car bearing No.KA-52-N-8506 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,338 of IPC.

Ex.P.5 is the wound certificate issued by Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital in which reason for the injuries suffered by the petitioner is noted as road traffic accident between two- wheeler and car on 09.08.2023 around 2.15 p.m. near Agarwal Hotel, Dasanapura, Nelamangala, Bengaluru.
18. In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of the police records regarding the reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 09.08.2023 at about 2.15 p.m. on Tumkur- Bengaluru NH-48 near Agarwal Bhawan Hotel, Dasanapura Hobli,
Nelamangala taluk, due to negligent use of motorcycle bearing No.KA-18-EG-3034 by the petitioner and negligent use of Car bearing No.KA-52-N- 8506 by Nagaraju at the ratio of 50:50 motorcycle dashed to the rear part of the car, thereby the accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 Accordingly.
19. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered right femur mid shaft fracture communited, closed, left distal radius volar barton fracture with carpal subluxation,
pelvic diastasis type II, deep penetrating laceration wounds over both inguinal regions and scrotum,
took treatment at Dhanvanthri hospital, Nelamangala, and Bhagawan Mahaveer Jain Hospital,
Bengaluru as inpatient from 09.08.2023 to 24.08.2023 by spending Rs.10,00,000/-, as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.30,000/-p.m. by working as Office Incharge at Truth Mining Claims company.
20.
In the written statement, respondent No.1 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
21. In the evidence petitioner produced medical bills worth of Rs.4,98,363/-.
In the cross-examination, petitioner denied the suggestion about non-spending of Rs.4,98,363/- towards treatment.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident he neither working as Office Assistant at Truth Mining Claims Company nor earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

22. In the evidence PW.2 produced copy of police intimation, MLC register extract, Inpatient file,
OPD book and CT Scan with report at Ex.P.13 to P.17.
23.
In the evidence PW.3 stated nothing regarding nature and consequences of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

Mohammed Feezan vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20168685/
4 24.

sentences.text: In the evidence PW.4- Dr. S.A. Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital stated that on 22.10.2024 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 64% to right lower limb which is about 32% to the whole body.
In the evidence PW.4 produced OPD Book and X-ray at Ex.P.19 and P.20.
In the cross-examination PW.4 admitted that he neither treated the petitioner nor verified inpatient treatment record nor collected opinion of the doctor who treated the petitioner.
PW.4 stated about verification of discharge summary.

25. Wound certificate, discharge summary, medical bills, prescriptions, X-ray, inpatient file and other medical records shows that in the accident petitioner suffered Polytrauma - right femur mid shaft fracture- comminuted closed, left distal radius volar barton fracture with carpal subluxation,
pelvic diastasis type 2, deep penetrating laceration wound over both inguinal regions and scrotum,
took treatment at Dhanavanthri Hospital, Nelamangala and Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital,
Bengaluru as inpatient from 09.08.2023 to 24.08.2023 by spending Rs.4,98,363/-.
In the file there are no documents regarding occupation and income of the petitioner.
26. In the Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P.8 the date birth of the petitioner is noted as 07.06.1990.
In the file there are no documents regarding decrease in the income of the petitioner or loss of income of the petitioner subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.
Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of PW.4 Dr.S.A. Somashekara is not sufficient to award compensation under the head loss of future income(Permanent Physical Disability).

27. Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of treatment taken by the petitioner, I asses compensation under the head pain and suffering at Rs.80,000/-, under the head of medical expenses at Rs.4,98,362/-, under the head of attendant conveyance and nourishment charges at Rs.20,000/-, under the head of loss of income during treatment period at Rs.96,000/- (Rs.16,000 x 6) and under the head of loss of amenities and future happiness at Rs.60,000/-.
28.
Hence, I assess total compensation of Rs.7,54,362/-.
In view of finding recorded in Issue No.1 the petitioner is entitle to receive compensation of Rs.3,77,181/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly.

Issue No.3:
29.
In the written statement, respondent No.1 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to the Car bearing No.KA-52-N-8506 as on the date of accident.
In this case there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident respondent No.2-owner of the Car violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-52-N-8506 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

sentences.text: The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.3,77,181/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Seventy seven thousand one hundred eighty one only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.1, being the Insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-52-N-8506 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
